_comment: The ISSB baseline itself, as a market row rather than a jurisdiction. IFRS S1
and S2 bind nobody on their own — a jurisdiction has to adopt them — which is
the single most misunderstood thing about the standard and the reason this
file exists rather than being folded into the others.
Adoption count is deliberately expressed as a floor, not a precise number:
jurisdictions move between 'adopted', 'aligned' and 'consulting' and no
reachable source gives a stable figure.
name: ISSB

sources.title: Use of IFRS Standards by jurisdiction

test: Nothing on its own. IFRS S2 applies where a jurisdiction has adopted or aligned to it — Australia and Singapore below are two such jurisdictions.

cohorts.name: Adopting jurisdictions
cohorts.also: Set by each jurisdiction, not by the ISSB
cohorts.note: More than 30 jurisdictions have adopted or aligned. The commencement date, the entities caught and the assurance requirement are all local decisions.

scope3: Required under paragraph 29(a), with a one-year transition relief allowing first-time reporters to omit it in year one.
assurance: Set by the adopting jurisdiction; the standard itself does not require it.
reliefs: First-year reliefs cover Scope 3, comparatives, and reporting timing relative to the financial statements.
digital_tagging: An IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy exists; mandating its use is a jurisdictional decision.
